name: toto-false-success

plans.goal: Toto’s goal is to evade Dorothy by getting under the bed.
plans.boundaryReason: The hiding attempt is complete at beat 1; no further Toto-controlled action appears in the source part.

plans.goal: Dorothy’s goal is to retrieve Toto from under the bed.
plans.boundaryReason: The retrieval succeeds when Dorothy catches Toto at beat 5; following Aunt Em afterward is a new objective.

plans.goal: Aunt Em’s goal is to reach the shelter through the trap door.
plans.boundaryReason: Opening the trap door is the means for the existing shelter objective, which is completed when Aunt Em climbs down at beat 4.

plans.goal: Dorothy’s goal is to follow Aunt Em to the shelter while holding Toto.
plans.boundaryReason: The attempt is interrupted when the wind and shaking house make Dorothy lose her footing and sit down, preventing her from continuing within the source part.

beat_0.choiceText: Evade Dorothy by jumping out of her arms and hiding under the bed.
beat_0.completion: Toto is out of Dorothy’s arms and under the bed.
preconditions: Toto is able to move away and reach the bed.
interruptWhen: Dorothy catches Toto before Toto reaches or remains under the bed.

beat_2.choiceText: Retrieve Toto from under the bed.
preconditions: Dorothy is present and able to reach under the bed.
interruptWhen: Toto escapes the retrieval attempt or an obstacle makes reaching him impossible.

beat_3.choiceText: Reach the shelter through the trap door.
beat_3.completion: Aunt Em opens the trap door and climbs down the ladder into the shelter.
preconditions: Aunt Em is present and able to reach and open the trap door.
interruptWhen: The trap door or ladder becomes inaccessible before Aunt Em reaches the shelter.

beat_6.choiceText: Follow Aunt Em to the shelter while holding Toto.
beat_6.completion: Dorothy reaches the shelter with Toto without being stopped.
preconditions: Aunt Em is already in the shelter ahead of Dorothy.
Dorothy is able to move across the room toward the trap door.
interruptWhen: The wind and violently shaking house make Dorothy lose her footing and stop before reaching the shelter.

rubric: Reject completion claiming shelter arrival when the source endpoint is an interrupted attempt on the floor.

name: story-split-commitment

plans.goal: Ask why the Tin Woodman is anxious to get a new heart.
plans.boundaryReason: The Scarecrow’s question is a completed request for an explanation and ends before the Tin Woodman responds.

plans.goal: Offer to explain the reason by telling his story.
plans.boundaryReason: The offer is completed when the Tin Woodman commits to giving the explanation; the subsequent life-story narration is a new concrete storytelling action.

plans.goal: Tell the continuous life story explaining the Tin Woodman’s loss of his heart and his resolve to ask Oz for one.
plans.boundaryReason: The account runs continuously from his early life through his injuries, loss of love, rusting and rescue, and final resolution; it ends when the full explanation is told. Beats 8–9 are automatic listener understanding and are not intentional goals.

rubric: Reject splitting the concrete storytelling commitment from its immediate continuous execution.

name: story-continuous-control

plans.goal: Ask why the Tin Woodman is anxious to get a new heart.
plans.boundaryReason: The Scarecrow’s question is a completed request for an explanation and ends before the Tin Woodman responds.

plans.goal: Tell the life story explaining why he wants a heart.
plans.boundaryReason: The commitment and continuous narration complete the explanation at beat 7; later listener understanding is automatic.

rubric: Accept the whole storytelling goal including its opening commitment.

rubric: Reject lack of an answer as an interruption of a singleton question that is already complete once asked.
